questions.stem: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is $10\text{ cm}$ and one angle is $30°$. What is the length of the side opposite to the $30°$ angle?
In a right-angled triangle, an angle is $40°$ and the adjacent side is $12\text{ cm}$. Which calculation finds the opposite side?
questions.explanation: We know the adjacent and want the opposite. $\tan 40° = \frac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}$, so opp $= \text{adj} \times \tan 40° = 12 \times \tan 40°$.
